cache_dump.note: ring_cache_keys.f32 holds layer 0's key rows [from_row, prefill_length + window) right after decode step 4 (the first ring-path write) as f32 [rows, kv_heads=10, head_dim=128] - a routing-independent lock on the ring slot arithmetic and written content.

ring.note: ring_logits.bf16 row i is the step kept_steps[i] decode logits row (the distribution producing forced token step+1); decode step 4 is the first written through the ring path (offset reaches prefill_length + window), so rows 4..8 lock the ring-overwrite attention semantics. The greedy top-6 routing margins per step (min over MoE layers, 6th vs 7th softmax score) are recorded in routing_min_margins: at margins below ~1e-3 the expert selection is not stable under the bf16-vs-f16 store drift, and the f16 port reproduces the branch exactly only up to the first such flip (step 4 here; verified by a per-layer bisection - layer inputs match to 4e-4 through the attention, and the divergence starts inside layer 1's MoE). Past the flip the two runs follow equally valid but different branches, so the Rust parity test pins the verified prefix and compares logits rows only within it.

notes: logits.bf16/ring_logits.bf16 hold the bf16 reference values bit-exactly; the Rust MLX port runs the same bf16 graph, so logits parity holds within a small kernel-order drift bound while greedy argmax tokens must match exactly. greedy_tokens is the forced 16-step argmax stream (EOS kept in-stream and flagged) because the production eos-aware loop emits EOS at step 0 on this synthetic noise input. Attention is LlamaAttention (qk_nope_head_dim=0 flips attn_type), MoE routing is softmax scoring with greedy top-6 and routed_scaling_factor 1.0, and logits go through the checkpoint's quantized lm_head (untied from embed_tokens).
